suggestions.assertion: Statistics are labelled as final career figures or carry an explicit as-of date with a named source
suggestions.reason: This is satisfiable by a one-line document preamble ('Compiled <date>. Figures are from X') with no label on the statistics table itself, which is what the without_skill run did. If the skill's 'Stats as of:' line in the identity header is the intended behaviour, the assertion should require the label to sit in the identity header or immediately adjacent to the stats table, and for retired players should require the words 'final career figures' explicitly.

suggestions.assertion: A numbered sources list gives at least three URLs
suggestions.reason: A bulleted list with exactly three URLs, where the other dozen entries name outlets without links, passes. Three URLs is a very low bar for a dossier with ~100 factual claims. Consider requiring that the headline statistics each cite a URL, or raising the minimum, or checking that the stats source named in the as-of line appears in the sources list.

Assertions 1–5 (birth date/place, 200/15,921, 463/18,426, 100 = 51 + 49, November 2013 retirement) are well-known reference facts that any competent model reproduces from memory; both runs passed all five. They verify the executor did not hallucinate but do not discriminate skill vs no-skill. Only the ratings-table assertion separated the two runs in this case.

No assertion checks internal consistency of the statistics. The with_skill dossier states '255 international catches' while its own fielding line (115 + 140 + 1) sums to 256. A check such as 'international catch total equals the sum of the per-format fielding figures' or 'the all-format aggregate (664 matches, 34,357 runs) equals the sum of the format rows' would catch this class of error.

No assertion covers the bowling table, the captaincy record, the career-arc section or the playing-style profile, all of which the skill mandates and the with_skill run produced. If those are required outputs of the skill, at least one assertion should check for them (e.g. 'ODI bowling row shows 154 wickets and best 5/32').

The two runs disagree on at least two facts (year Root passed the fourth-innings-runs record: 2024 vs January 2026; Padma Shri year: 1998 vs 1999). No assertion checks either, and the grader cannot resolve them without web access. If record-status currency matters to this skill, an assertion pinning one such post-2013 fact would be discriminating.

eval_feedback.overall: All 8 assertions pass on substance, not surface compliance: the with_skill dossier has the required identity header, correctly populated stat rows, an 8-row ratings table with justifications, an explicit 'Final career figures' label with named sources, and 20 numbered sources with 43 URLs. The assertion set itself is weak at discriminating: five of eight are memorised-fact checks that both runs pass, and the as-of and sources assertions are satisfiable by minimal effort. One internal arithmetic error (255 vs 256 catches) and two cross-run factual conflicts went uncaught by the assertions.
